name: Chapel infirmary (Tobin's sickroom)
region: Top of Chapel Lane, sick village

sensoryProfile.sight: Squat grey house of the Light with a bell-cote and no bell; benches carried out and stacked upside down in the yard under the yew; inside dim, close and too warm with every shutter barred except one: a round of thick greenish glass above the altar in little bubbled panes, facing down the lane, with one pane wiped clear of soot. A brazier smokes in the middle of the floor; round it, packed side to side, every bed that could be carried (cots, a box bed with its doors off, a child's truckle bed, a door laid across two trestles with a straw pallet) under blankets 'every colour there was'; some beds made up empty. A stone font. A cracked slate in a wooden frame hung on a nail inside the door.
sensoryProfile.sound: Coughing; a child saying 'Mam, Mam, Mam' in a small flat voice; the brazier spitting; Garran's breath catching 'at the top'.
sensoryProfile.smell: Vinegar first, sweat, tallow, an unemptied slop bucket; under it all a faint thick sweetness: pears gone brown.
sensoryProfile.touch: Warm, close; cold running out of the ash staff into the hands and chest; gritty doorframe.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: A house made into a ward: too many lamps and one taper. Over every bed the thin blue shine of Jaina's wards, fed round by round.

establishedFacts.fact: Tobin has had the benches carried out and the village's beds put in; Garran and Elsie are at opposite ends (truckle bed and door-bed under the window). Chapel window above the altar faces down the lane to the granary and bakehouse: Jaina watches Sylvanas there.

Patients (chapter end): Garran (late), Elsie, the cooper's boy, the cooper's wife, Col, Wenna Dunmore (with Hew), a little girl in a man's coat who sits by the font. Beds kept for the cooper's three more.

eventsHere.event: Jaina's rounds of readings and wards; the slate; the bread deduction; Lyriel's knot lesson; Sylvanas's dusk report; night vigil; Lyriel rebinds Jaina's hand; Mother Haw's oatcakes arrive; dawn: Elsie's forehead cool.
